---
title: "Drought indices: SPI and SPEI"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The standardised precipitation index (SPI) says how unusual the precipitation
of the last months is, in standard deviations, compared with the same months
in other years at the same place. An SPI of -1.5 over three months means a
dry spell of a severity seen about once every 15 years. The SPEI does the
same with the water balance: precipitation minus potential
evapotranspiration.

```{r setup}
library(c4e)

survey <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "survey.csv", package = "c4e"))
survey$interview <- as.Date(survey$interview)
coord <- prepare_coord(survey, lat_var = lat, lon_var = lon,
                       id = hhid, interview = interview)
```

## Monthly data, a long series

The indices need monthly data and many years: the package ships forty years
of monthly precipitation. Daily data are first summed to months with
`aggregate_time()`.

```{r data}
pre <- read_climate(system.file("extdata", "pre_monthly.tif", package = "c4e"))
raster_meta(pre)[c("variable", "unit", "time_step", "date_range")]
extracted <- extract_by_coord(pre, georef_coord(coord))
```

## The index

`calc_std_index()` fits the index at one or more accumulation scales, in
months. Each series is fitted on its own location's history.

```{r spi}
spi <- calc_std_index(extracted, scale = c(3, 12))
dplyr::filter(spi, ID == ID[1], date >= as.Date("2022-01-01")) |> head(6)
```

```{r plot}
one <- dplyr::filter(spi, ID == ID[1], date >= as.Date("2015-01-01"))
plot(one$date, one$spi_3, type = "h", col = ifelse(one$spi_3 < 0, "firebrick", "steelblue"),
     xlab = NULL, ylab = "SPI-3", main = "Three-month SPI at one location")
abline(h = c(-1, -1.5), lty = 2)
```

## Drought months and spells

`calc_std_threshold()` flags the months beyond index thresholds. The sign
stays in the column name, so `spi3_blw_-1.5` is the months with a
three-month SPI below -1.5. The flags work with spells like any other.

```{r thresholds}
dry <- calc_std_threshold(spi, below = c(-1, -1.5))
dry <- calc_spell(dry, min_spell = 2)
names(dry)
```

## Before each interview

```{r summary}
summary <- summarise_by_interview(coord, dry, window = window_lag("1 year"))
print(summary, n = 4)
c4e_labels(summary)[c("spi_3_mean", "spi3_blw_-1.5_sum")]
```

## The SPEI

With potential evapotranspiration, the same function gives the SPEI. Here a
constant 60 mm a month stands in for it; ERA5 records evapotranspiration as
a negative number, and either sign is accepted.

```{r spei}
pet <- dplyr::mutate(extracted, dplyr::across(dplyr::matches("^\\d{4}-"), \(v) v * 0 + 60))
spei <- calc_std_index(extracted, scale = 3, index = "spei", pet = pet)
names(spei)
```

## In one call

`climate_indices()` runs the chain from the survey and the raster; daily
precipitation is summed to months by itself.

```{r wrapper}
drought <- climate_indices(survey, system.file("extdata", "pre_monthly.tif", package = "c4e"),
                           id = hhid, interview = interview, scale = c(3, 12),
                           control = indices_control(verbose = FALSE))
print(drought, n = 4)
```
